notes.title: A date at picture scale
notes.body: The huge ’70 dominates the upper half. It is part of the title and the period being named; it is not an edition date.

notes.title: A group with individual rhythms
notes.body: Eight figures appear side by side, with bent arms and feet at differing heights. Their poses suggest movement without proving that every figure is running.

notes.title: Three dates to keep apart
notes.body: The novel dates to 1983, this reprint to 2019, and the title names the 1970s. These dates answer different questions.

studyData.intro: A decade becomes a huge heading above a compact group of moving figures. Follow the details to compare what is visible, what can be interpreted and what the edition record establishes.

regions.label: Two huge numerals name a decade
regions.summary: The numerals ’70 occupy much of the upper-middle cover in pale thin strokes.
regions.question: What changes if you mistake ’70 for the date this copy was published?

sections.heading: Large ’70 in the image
sections.body: The numerals ’70 occupy much of the upper-middle cover in pale thin strokes. Their large open spaces allow the taupe field to remain visible. The apostrophe and sweeping 7 give this enormous title element a more fluid rhythm than a compact date stamp.

sections.heading: A decade towers above individual bodies
sections.body: The number refers to the decade named by the book, not the printing date. Its enormous size gives historical time visual weight. Compare the numerals with the small human figures below: the cover places a broad period above individual bodies.

sections.heading: A novel and a later adaptation
sections.body: The Cultural Center of the Philippines dates Bautista’s novel to 1983 and the film adaptation to 2002. These are separate historical events from the 1970s named in the title and the 2019 reprint shown here. The large numerals should therefore be read as subject matter, not production metadata.

regions.label: A long word forms the upper line
regions.summary: Dekada stretches almost the full width near the top.
regions.question: Can a thin line be visually dominant, and what does this title show you about that?

sections.heading: Dekada lettering in the image
sections.body: Dekada stretches almost the full width near the top. Its pale strokes are slender, with rounded endings and generous internal spaces. The lettering occupies a large area while leaving much of the background visible through and around its forms.

sections.heading: Thin strokes claim a large space
sections.body: Dekada means decade. Its long horizontal line and the tall numerals beneath work together as a title rather than two unrelated labels. Compare the lightness of the thin strokes with the amount of space the title claims on the page.

regions.label: Eight figures share a direction
regions.summary: Eight illustrated figures stand or move side by side below the title.
regions.question: What makes these eight figures feel connected without making them identical?

sections.heading: Eight figures in the image
sections.body: Eight illustrated figures stand or move side by side below the title. Their heads, shoulders and bent arms make an uneven line. Differing clothes and body positions keep them distinct even where neighbouring outlines touch or overlap.

sections.heading: A group moves without becoming uniform
sections.body: Their repeated forward-facing orientation suggests a group, while their unequal poses resist perfect uniformity. Some feet are raised and some legs look more upright, so movement is clearer than a claim that everyone is running in exactly the same way.

regions.label: Different foot heights create rhythm
regions.summary: The lower silhouettes alternate between long straight legs, bent rear legs and feet at different heights.
regions.question: Which pair of legs gives the clearest evidence of a step or stride?

sections.heading: Feet and steps in the image
sections.body: The lower silhouettes alternate between long straight legs, bent rear legs and feet at different heights. Shoes and stockings vary in tone. The ground remains visible between the bodies, and those irregular gaps help distinguish one pose from the next.

sections.heading: Read the movement through the shoes
sections.body: The changes in height create a rhythm that can suggest movement across a still image. Looking only at the shoes produces a different reading from looking only at the faces. Compare both before naming a specific action for the entire group.

regions.label: Colour distinguishes neighbours
regions.summary: Blue, red, grey and dark garments alternate across the group.
regions.question: Which two neighbouring figures would be hardest to separate if their clothes had the same colour?

sections.heading: Clothing colours in the image
sections.body: Blue, red, grey and dark garments alternate across the group. Some figures wear jackets, others short sleeves, shorts or long trousers. These colour blocks are small compared with the title but contain much of the cover’s concentrated variation.

sections.heading: Clothes distinguish bodies, not fixed identities
sections.body: Clothes help the eye separate adjacent bodies. They do not, on their own, establish occupation, class or a precise identity for each person. Describe the visible differences first, then distinguish any story-based interpretation from what the picture actually supplies.

regions.label: A pale field opens behind the group
regions.summary: Pale cloud-like sweeps spread outward behind the figures.
regions.question: Where does the pale background most clearly reveal a person’s outline?

sections.heading: Pale background in the image
sections.body: Pale cloud-like sweeps spread outward behind the figures. Their soft, mottled edges differ from the darker outlined bodies. The pale shapes rise at the sides while leaving a quieter central area beneath the huge numerals.

sections.heading: A pale field makes the figures stand out
sections.body: The background can suggest atmosphere or movement without becoming a precisely identified weather event. Its strongest practical effect is contrast: the darker group becomes easier to recognise. Compare the figures against the pale area and against the darker ground below.

regions.label: A small line describes the edition
regions.summary: Ang Orihinal at Kumpletong Edisyon appears between the large title and the figures.
regions.question: Why does this phrase not automatically make the shown copy a first edition?

sections.heading: Edition wording in the image
sections.body: Ang Orihinal at Kumpletong Edisyon appears between the large title and the figures. The phrase means the original and complete edition. Its modest size and straight baseline distinguish it from the more expressive title lettering above.

sections.heading: An original text can appear in a later reprint
sections.body: The line is a statement printed on this cover, not proof that this copy is the first printing. A later reprint can present an original and complete text. Separating wording about the text from publication metadata prevents two different senses of original from being confused.

regions.label: The writer’s name forms a lower anchor
regions.summary: LUALHATI BAUTISTA appears in two large pale lines near the bottom.
regions.question: How does the author block differ in weight from the title despite sharing a pale colour?

sections.heading: Author name in the image
sections.body: LUALHATI BAUTISTA appears in two large pale lines near the bottom. Broad capital letters contrast with the thin, flowing title above. A sizeable area of ground separates the name from the figures, giving it its own clear block.

sections.heading: A steady name beneath an uneven group
sections.body: The name stabilises the lower cover after the uneven rhythm of the group. Its pale colour links it back to the title while its heavier forms provide a different emphasis. This hierarchy gives authorship a substantial presence without adding another illustration.

regions.label: A burgundy corner identifies a series
regions.summary: A burgundy rectangle occupies the upper-right corner, containing a pale emblem and ANVIL CLASSICS wording.
regions.question: What does the corner tell a browsing reader that the main title does not?

sections.heading: Anvil Classics in the image
sections.body: A burgundy rectangle occupies the upper-right corner, containing a pale emblem and ANVIL CLASSICS wording. Its straight edges and dense colour distinguish it from the thin title strokes. The device is partly aligned with the outer border rather than the central group.

sections.heading: Separate the 1970s, the 1983 novel and the 2019 reprint
sections.body: Ayala Museum Shop identifies the shown book as Anvil’s 2019 reprint, ISBN 9789712733987. The Cultural Center of the Philippines dates the novel to 1983. Neither record makes the large ’70 an edition date or identifies this cover’s designer.

regions.label: A pale edge holds the composition
regions.summary: A light border surrounds the taupe central panel.
regions.question: Which edge details belong to the reproduced object rather than clearly to its designed layout?

sections.heading: Pale border in the image
sections.body: A light border surrounds the taupe central panel. Its width is not perfectly even in this photographed copy, and a narrow crease-like line is visible near the left side. The edge separates the printed composition from the image boundary.

sections.heading: A printed enclosure and a physical copy
sections.body: The border gives the large title and small group a shared enclosure. Visible surface marks also remind us that this is a reproduction of a copy, not a pristine design file. Avoid treating every crease or tonal variation as an intentional graphic decision.

connections.title: A decade above individual bodies
connections.label: Decade / people
connections.text: Huge thin numerals name a historical period above eight much smaller figures, contrasting the scale of a decade with individual bodies.

connections.title: Two scales of identity
connections.label: Group / author
connections.text: Distinct clothing separates people within the small group, while the large pale author name supplies a different kind of identification below.
